topic: dsh-trace-compare Guide 2026: Visualizing Agent Exploration Paths in DeepSeek Harness

key_points: dsh-trace-compare was RENAMED to dsh-maze as of v1.0.0 — the old npm package (dsh-trace-compare@0.7.0) is frozen and feature-identical to dsh-maze 1.0.0; only dsh-maze moves forward (now at 2.1.0)

The 'execution maze': main path, failed detours and backtracks on ONE timeline — solid line = successful tool steps plus answer nodes; dashed arcs = exploration detours (red ✗ tool failed, gray · searched and found nothing, gray ↻ blind retry) with the return arc back to the branch point
Duration capsules: every step renders as a verdict-colored rounded bar spanning start→end (a 3-min bash vs a 0.2s read are visually distinct; wide bars carry duration inline)
Parallel tool-call rows (v0.3.2+): steps firing >=2 tool calls render each call as a thin waterfall bar with real start/end and verdict coloring

Data tracks: per-step tool-call density, token pulse (cached-backdrop + uncached-input/reasoning/output bars), context pressure (70%/90% threshold lines, compaction events marked); tracks with no usage in the log are not drawn — honesty rule
Execution analysis (v0.7): duration scatter plot (per-tool P50/P95 reference lines), per-tool result matrix, failure recovery chains (identical retry / changed args / switched tool / not recovered)
Multi-session compare (the core 'trace compare'): 2-5 runs of the same task on one shared axis with turn-alignment lines, manual anchors, and a per-turn detour inventory with time deltas
Replay up to 300x; export current view as SVG or 2x PNG (always light-background)

House rules: every number is a deterministic aggregation over judged data — NO LLM involved; every verdict carries a rationale; every conclusion traces back to evidence; missing data is labeled honestly, never invented
Two entries: the Live Maze tab inside every session (grows live) and Maze in the sidebar (upload session logs to inspect or compare)
Comparable but different goal: side-by-side MULTI-MODEL evaluation inside DeepSeek Harness, not trace visualization — one prompt runs concurrently across 2-4 model routes in isolated Git worktrees
Streams live tool trajectories per model; shows compact elapsed-time and tool-count summaries with token/cache/TTFT/decoding details
Turn-alignment/detour comparison is dsh-maze's province; dsh-dual-model-eval focuses on which model produces an adoptable result
First release targets Harness 0.1.0-rc.7; plugin APIs may change between release candidates (developer-preview caveat)
OpenTelemetry tracing/metrics/logging for DeepSeek Harness runs exported to GreptimeDB with seven Grafana dashboards — a telemetry/backend pipeline, not a timeline visualization
Answers cost, tokens, money, time; dsh-maze answers exploration structure and wasted steps
Positions DSH observability as an existing-ecosystem (OTel/Grafana) problem vs dsh-maze's standalone interactive maze
Langfuse telemetry sidecar bundle for DeepSeek Harness — exports agent sessions to Langfuse for LLM observability (trace/span/cost dashboards)
Represents the LLM-tracing approach (centralized backend, per-call spans); complementary to — not a replacement for — structural exploration visualization
Shows DSH's observability ecosystem is fragmented: telemetry backends (Langfuse/LangSmith) vs visualization plugins (dsh-maze)
Official DeepSeek Harness developer-preview page: 'Everything is a plugin' built on the Cordis kernel
Every run is traceable via an append-only session log with a built-in Trajectory view — this is the baseline the dsh-maze plugin enhances
Four runtime modes: Standard, Code, Minimal, Creator; quick start npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web (defaults to http://127.0.0.1:3080)
Provides the 'why': agents explore, detour, backtrack, and fail — visualizing that exploration is the value the harness itself hints at but dsh-maze makes explicit

stats.fact: dsh-trace-compare was renamed to dsh-maze at v1.0.0; the old package is frozen at v0.7.0 (feature-identical to dsh-maze 1.0.0) with only dsh-maze moving forward — current version 2.1.0 (updated 2026-09-04).

Install is two commands after setup: 'dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-maze' then 'dsh web'; after restart the sidebar gains a Maze entry and every session view gains a Live Maze tab. Migration from the old name: 'dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-trace-compare' then 'dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-maze'.

Version pinning matters: hosts on the 0.1.2 line (DSH Desktop 2.x, npm @deepseek-ai/dsh@next 0.1.2-rc.1, or self-built master) should install dsh-maze 2.x (tag latest); older hosts (npm latest 0.1.0-rc.6 ~ 0.1.1-rc.2) must pin dsh-maze@1.1.0. Host 0.1.2 re-split its client packages (dsh-client-runtime became dsh-client-store and friends).
dsh-maze is MIT-licensed, written in HTML/JS, 65 stars as of 2026-09-04, created 2026-08-18; topics include agent-observability, agent-trajectory, dsh, dsh-plugin, maze, trace, visualization.

Every number in dsh-maze is a deterministic aggregation over judged data — no LLM is invoked; verdicts layer error flags -> failure signatures -> per-tool-class rules, and each verdict carries a rationale string (blind retries are counted only for consecutive same-tool similar-args clusters containing a failure, following AgentLens-style deterministic waste detection for SWE-agent trajectories).

Upload accepts plain .jsonl (session format v0 event streams) and .jsonl.zstd exactly as stored under ~/.dsh/sessions/, decompressed in the browser; detection is by content, so the file name does not matter.

Honesty rules: idle stretches over 60s collapse into thin pause seams; token counts come from assistant/message usage (logs without usage fall back to an honest 'reasoning N chunks' label); failure-signature scans only head/tail windows to ignore error-looking text quoted mid-output; missing-data tracks are not drawn.

The official DeepSeek Harness records every run in an append-only session log (system prompts, reasoning, tool calls, subagent scheduling) viewable in the built-in Trajectory view — the data dsh-maze visualizes.

angles: 'Trace compare' is a NEW distinct capability: comparing MULTIPLE runs of the same task on one axis — not just reading one session — to see which model/run explored less, backtracked less, and wasted less wall-clock time
The rename dsh-trace-compare -> dsh-maze signals the tool's evolution from compare-focused to a full visualization suite (maze + data tracks + execution analysis + compare + replay)
Honesty by design: deterministic aggregation with no LLM in the loop, evidence-backed verdicts, and labeled gaps — a trust angle that matters for agent debugging and evaluation
Version pinning nightmare in developer preview: plugin versions must match host line (0.1.2 vs older), echoing the broader DeepSeek Harness compatibility-breaking rapid-iteration caveat
Exploration as a quality signal: failed detours, blind retries, and dead-ends quantify agent efficiency and wasted cost — visualization makes 'how much did the agent meander' measurable
Complement vs competition with telemetry backends (Langfuse/LangSmith via dsh plugins) and OpenTelemetry exporters — dsh-maze is the structural/timeline viewer, not a metrics backend
Direct relevance to our own pipeline: we run DeepSeek Harness, so visualizing our own agent exploration paths is actionable for debugging and model evaluation
